step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture shows OLX Autos' developer platform (Orion) which enables global expansion across 11 countries. End-users access the portal via Route 53, which routes traffic through an Application Load Balancer (ALB) to an Amazon EKS cluster running the main application pods. To minimize costs, 100% of the workloads are executed on EC2 Spot Instances. To manage spot terminations and ensure state consistency during provisioning jobs, EKS deploys the AWS Node Termination Handler. In addition, when microservice provisioning jobs are launched on Spot instances, they register their progress by publishing events to Amazon SNS, which are then fanned out to Amazon SQS. If a Spot instance is terminated before completion, a newly scheduled replacement job polls SQS to pick up the unfinished tasks and resume gracefully.

graph.name: OLX Autos - Resilient Environment Provisioning on EKS with 100% Spot Instances
graph.notes: Main portal backend running on EKS orchestrates environment creation by triggering Kubernetes jobs on EC2 Spot Instances. By persisting state through SNS and SQS, replacement jobs can resume unfinished provisioning tasks when Spot nodes are terminated, achieving resilience with 100% Spot instances.

nodes.name: End User
nodes.notes: Accesses the Orion portal to trigger environment creation requests.

nodes.name: Amazon Route 53
nodes.notes: Resolves DNS requests for the Orion platform.

nodes.name: Application Load Balancer
nodes.notes: Distributes incoming traffic to the backend services on the Kubernetes cluster.

nodes.name: Amazon EKS
nodes.notes: Orchestrates microservices and Kubernetes jobs. Scaled from 100 pods to over 10,000 pods.

nodes.name: EC2 Spot Instances
nodes.notes: Hosts 100% of the application and provisioning jobs to optimize costs. Employs AWS Node Termination Handler to drain nodes gracefully.

nodes.name: Amazon SNS
nodes.notes: Receives launch progress and state registration events from the microservice provisioning jobs.

nodes.name: Amazon SQS
nodes.notes: Holds persistent queue messages of unfinished provisioning tasks.

edges.notes: User requests Orion portal domain resolution.
Route 53 resolves traffic to the ALB.
ALB forwards the environment creation requests to the main application pod on EKS.
EKS schedules microservice provisioning jobs onto EC2 Spot Instances.
Provisioning jobs publish progress and initialization status to SNS.
SNS fans out execution state and status events to SQS.
Newly scheduled replacement jobs on EC2 Spot watch SQS to fetch unfinished tasks and resume provisioning state.
